BayesSpace parameters

Source: R/tool-bayesspace.R
bayesspaceParam.Rd

Parameters for GiottoClass::clusterData() that run BayesSpace (Zhao et al. 2021), which clusters spots of array-based spatial transcriptomics (Visium, ST, Visium HD bins) with a Bayesian model whose Potts prior favours the same cluster for neighbouring spots. BayesSpace is a Bioconductor package (BiocManager::install("BayesSpace")). If you use it, please cite the original paper (see References).

Usage

bayesspaceParam(
  q,
  platform = c("Visium", "ST", "VisiumHD"),
  d = 15L,
  n_pcs = 15L,
  n_hvgs = 2000L,
  log_normalize = TRUE,
  init_method = c("mclust", "kmeans"),
  model = c("t", "normal"),
  precision = c("equal", "variable"),
  nrep = 50000L,
  burn_in = 1000L,
  thin = 100L,
  gamma = NULL,
  mu0 = NULL,
  lambda0 = NULL,
  alpha = 1,
  beta = 0.01,
  seed = 1234L
)

# S4 method for class 'allMatrix,bayesspaceParam'
clusterData(x, param, spatial_locs, pcs = NULL, ...)

Arguments

q

integer, number of clusters (no default in BayesSpace; its qTune() helps choose one)

platform

"Visium" (hexagonal grid, 6 neighbours), "ST" or "VisiumHD" (square grid, 4 neighbours)

d

integer, number of principal components used

n_pcs, n_hvgs

integer, components and highly variable genes of BayesSpace's preprocessing (spatialPreprocess()); not used when a stored dimension reduction is given

log_normalize

logical, log-normalize counts before the PCA

init_method

"mclust" or "kmeans", initial clustering

model

"t" or "normal", error model

precision

"equal" or "variable", cluster covariance

nrep, burn_in, thin

integer, MCMC iterations, burn-in and thinning

gamma

numeric, smoothing strength; NULL uses BayesSpace's default (3 for Visium, 2 otherwise)

mu0, lambda0

prior mean and precision of the cluster means; NULL uses BayesSpace's defaults

alpha, beta

numeric, priors of the t-model scaling

seed

integer seed set before preprocessing and clustering; NULL leaves the random state alone

x

count matrix, features x cells (dense or sparse)

spatial_locs

data.frame with cell_ID and either the array grid positions array_row, array_col or the coordinates sdimx, sdimy (the grid is then derived from the spot spacing)

pcs

optional matrix, cells x dimensions (rownames are cell IDs) to cluster on instead of BayesSpace's own preprocessing

Value

A bayesspaceParam object.

Details

clusterData(x, param, spatial_locs) returns a data.table with cell_ID, cluster (BayesSpace's spatial.cluster) and cluster_init (the initial non-spatial clustering). Its attributes pcs (the components clustered) and hvf (BayesSpace's highly variable features, when it preprocessed) hold the intermediate results.

References

Zhao E, Stone MR, Ren X, Guenthoer J, Smythe KS, Pulliam T, Williams SR, Uytingco CR, Taylor SEB, Nghiem P, Bielas JH, Gottardo R. Spatial transcriptomics at subspot resolution with BayesSpace. Nature Biotechnology 39, 1375-1384 (2021). doi:10.1038/s41587-021-00935-2

See also

runBayesSpace()

Examples

p <- bayesspaceParam(q = 7, nrep = 10000)
p$q
